entries.mechanism: A tensor is a bifunctor with unit object and coherent invertible natural unitors and associator; braiding or symmetry requires cross-tensor arrows
entries.use: M1-A/M1-C derive necessary weak-unitor equations; M2-A/M2-B verify actual monoidal countermodels and a typed empty-hom obstruction
entries.adaptation: The discrete object's monoid is noncommutative; a C2 loop factor supplies nonidentity arrows. All changed assumptions and coherence checks are explicit.
entries.boundary: An omitted tensor field is not nonexistence evidence; no claim excludes a monoidal enlargement or all alternative tensors on the M2 categories

entries.actually_read: The passage beginning 'First, suppose we have any monoidal category', through the End(I) commutativity and interchange argument; HTML lines89-135 in retrieved text
entries.mechanism: Composition and tensor on endomorphisms of the monoidal unit agree and commute by common-unit interchange
entries.use: M1-B and M1-C; explicit two substitutions prove the general operation theorem, then contradict reset-map noncommutativity
entries.adaptation: For the concrete unchanged one-object category, only identity is invertible, so arbitrary weak unitors reduce to identity before applying the operation theorem
entries.boundary: Strictness is derived for this countermodel; it is not assumed for arbitrary monoidal categories. No novelty claim.
